issue: Does a noncitizen who entered without admission and is present in the United States count as 'seeking admission' under 8 U.S.C. § 1225(b)(2)(A), so that mandatory detention applies rather than a bond hearing under § 1226(a)?

sides.position: Noncitizens present without admission are 'applicants for admission' subject to mandatory detention under § 1225(b)(2)(A) and are not entitled to a bond hearing
A noncitizen present without admission is not 'seeking admission' under § 1225(b)(2)(A) and is eligible for a bond hearing under § 1226(a)
cases: Rhoney v. Barbosa da Cunha (2d Cir.)

this_court: The Seventh Circuit takes the position that the noncitizen is not 'seeking admission' and is eligible for a § 1226(a) bond hearing, so it is not subject to mandatory detention under § 1225(b)(2)(A).
quote: We share the dissent's hope that the Supreme Court will settle this matter and bring uniformity.
cite: Jaciel Rojas v. Samuel Olson, No. 25-3127 (7th Cir. 2026)
